decisions.reason: The formal statement and proof correctly require T to be bounded, but the displayed title omitted that indispensable hypothesis. An unbounded linear functional has one-dimensional range and cannot be compact because the local compact-operator definition implies boundedness. The title and its batch-page metadata now say bounded finite rank; the proof itself needed no change.

The example cited a definition restricted to real-valued sequences while quantifying over both real and complex diagonals. The mathematics was otherwise sound. The statement now types a as a function N->K, explicitly defines boundedness in modulus and the epsilon meaning of a_n->0, and no longer declares the real-only sequence item as a dependency.

Step 2.2 incorrectly included an arbitrary nonzero center lambda in the spectrum, although the corollary quantifies over all nonzero complex lambda. The isolation conclusion still follows from finiteness after replacing the local spectral set by its difference with {lambda}; the repaired minimum-distance argument now covers both lambda in the spectrum and lambda outside it.

The reverse implication used the symbol ||S|| without declaring the operator-norm interface. Boundedness already supplies a real bound b with ||Sy||<=b||y||, so the repaired proof chooses such b and uses C=max(b,1) in the compact-remainder estimate. This fixes the contract without adding an unnecessary dependency.

Fact F6 overstated its supplier by saying every finite exponent, which includes 0<p<1, while the supplied density theorem states 1<=p<infinity. The proof uses only p=2, so its conclusion remains valid. F6 now reproduces the exact range, and the simple-function approximants have also been made type-explicit as indicators of finite rectangle unions.

reviews.reason: After the title repair, the statement assumes a bounded linear map and the proof places the unit-ball image inside ||T|| times the compact unit ball of its closed finite-dimensional range. Closure inside that compact set proves compactness, including the zero-operator case. Focused precheck passed.

The repaired proof first covers the nonzero spectrum by countably many finite annular sets. For arbitrary nonzero lambda it removes lambda from the finite local spectral set, takes the positive minimum distance when nonempty, and otherwise uses |lambda|/2; the resulting ball has no spectral point other than possibly lambda. Focused precheck passed.

For both scalar fields, finite-rank truncations have exact tail operator norm, convergence of a to zero gives a norm limit of compact operators, and failure of convergence yields a DC-chosen subsequence whose diagonal images are uniformly separated. I also corrected the separation estimate from equality to a lower bound and fixed the infinite-support boundary metadata. Focused precheck passed.

With a chosen bound for S, the compact-remainder lemma gives finite kernel and closed range. Transposing the second compact remainder embeds ker(T*) in the finite-dimensional kernel of identity minus a compact operator; quotient duality and dual separation then make the cokernel finite dimensional. The forward parametrix direction is unchanged. Focused precheck passed.

At p=2, finite simple functions reduce density to indicators of finite-measure sets. Sigma-finite rectangle exhaustions and generating-algebra approximation provide finite rectangle unions in the base product; completed-measurable indicators first receive base-measurable representatives. The coefficient estimates now omit zero values and consistently use indicator functions. Focused precheck passed.
